name: Telomere Dynamics, Telomerase Regulation, and Cellular Senescence

reference.source: Medical Biochemistry 5th ed / Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd ed
clinicalPearls: Telomeres comprise tandem TTAGGG repeats capped by the six-protein shelterin complex to prevent DNA damage signaling
The end-replication problem causes somatic telomere erosion, enforcing the Hayflick limit and replicative senescence
Telomerase (hTERT + hTERC RNA template) is repressed in somatic tissues but reactivated in >85-90% of human cancers
Senescent cells exhibit the SASP (senescence-associated secretory phenotype), secreting IL-6, IL-8, and matrix proteases
Dyskeratosis congenita is an inherited telomeropathy causing oral leukoplakia, nail dystrophy, and fatal aplastic anemia
reference.pathophysiology: Inability of DNA polymerases to replicate the extreme 5'-terminus of the lagging strand leads to progressive telomere attrition with each cell division. Once telomeres reach a critical threshold, uncapped chromosome ends trigger persistent p53-dependent DNA damage responses, driving cells into irreversible senescence or apoptosis. Reactivation of telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) bypasses this barrier, conferring infinite replicative potential in malignant neoplasms.
additionalDifferentials: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and familial bone marrow failure syndromes
Werner syndrome (adult progeria due to WRN RecQ DNA helicase defect)
Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome (LMNA lamin A mutation / progerin)
additionalInvestigations: Flow-FISH (fluorescence in situ hybridization) for leukocyte telomere length measurement
TRAP assay (telomeric repeat amplification protocol) for telomerase enzymatic activity
Targeted gene panel sequencing for telomeropathy genes (DKC1, TERC, TERT, TINF2)
Senescence-associated beta-galactosidase (SA-beta-gal) staining on tissue sections
